A continuous trait whose rate of evolution varies among branches

Source: R/traits_rates.R
trait_rates.Rd

Simulates Brownian motion in which each branch has its own rate (variance per unit time), and keeps those rates, so that methods which estimate rates per branch can be compared with the rates that generated the data. Three models of how rates vary are available:

Usage

trait_rates(
  tree,
  model = c("shift", "gbm", "iid"),
  sigma2 = 1,
  shifts = 1,
  shift_size = 4,
  shift_edges = NULL,
  shift_rate = NULL,
  shift_branch = FALSE,
  relative = TRUE,
  rate_sd = 0.5,
  root = 0,
  edge_rates = NULL,
  root_value = NULL
)

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree with branch lengths.

model

How rates vary among branches: "shift", "gbm" or "iid".

sigma2

Rate at the root ("shift", "gbm") or median rate ("iid").

shifts

Number of shifts, for "shift" when neither shift_edges nor shift_rate is given.

shift_size

Multipliers of the rate at each shift, recycled to the number of shifts, or a function of the number of shifts that gives them. Values below 1 slow evolution down.

shift_edges

Optional row numbers of tree$edge at whose start the shifts happen.

shift_rate

Optional rate of shifts per unit of branch length, for shifts as a Poisson process along the branches.

shift_branch

Should a shift last only to the end of its branch, rather than pass to all branches descending from it?

relative

Multiply the rate before each shift by shift_size (TRUE), or set the rate after it to sigma2 times shift_size (FALSE)?

rate_sd

Standard deviation of the logarithm of the rate: per square root of time for "gbm" and among branches for "iid".

root

Trait value at the root.

edge_rates

Optional rate of each branch, in the order of the rows of tree$edge, such as those of history_rates(). When given, model and its arguments are ignored.

root_value

Deprecated; use root.

Value

A list with

  • tips: the trait at the tips, named by species;

  • nodes: the trait at the internal nodes, named by their numbers in tree$edge, the root first;

  • edge_rates: the rate of each branch, in the order of the rows of tree$edge, as in trait_mk() (also as edge_rate, its name before 0.7.0, until 1.0.0);

  • node_rate: for "gbm", the rate at every node, tips first, named by node number; NULL otherwise;

  • shifts: for "shift", a data frame with the edge (row of tree$edge), the node at its end, the position of the shift as time from the start of the edge, the multiplier and the rate after the shift; NULL otherwise;

  • tree: the tree given, and scaled: the tree with each branch length multiplied by its rate, under which the trait is ordinary Brownian motion.

Details

  • "shift": the rate is sigma2 at the root and changes at a few points of the tree. With shift_branch = FALSE the new rate is inherited by every branch descending from the shift, as in the models of Eastman et al. (2011), traitMedusa in motmot (Thomas & Freckleton 2012), BAMM (Rabosky 2014) or bifrost; with shift_branch = TRUE it lasts only to the end of the branch. By default shifts shifts happen at the start of branches drawn with probabilities proportional to their length, or of the branches in shift_edges. With shift_rate, shifts instead happen as a Poisson process along the branches, as under the prior of BAMM: their number is Poisson with mean shift_rate times the total length of the tree, and they fall at uniform positions over it, so also within branches. At each shift the rate is multiplied by shift_size (relative = TRUE), or becomes sigma2 times shift_size whatever it was before (relative = FALSE), as each new regime of BAMM or bifrost has a rate of its own. shift_size can be a function of the number of shifts that draws them, such as function(n) stats::rlnorm(n, 0, 1). The rate of a branch is its mean over the branch, weighted by time.

  • "gbm": the logarithm of the rate evolves itself by Brownian motion with standard deviation rate_sd per square root of time, starting from log(sigma2) at the root, as in the variable-rate models of Revell (2021) and Martin et al. (2023). The rate of a branch is the geometric mean of the rates at its two ends.

  • "iid": the rate of each branch is sigma2 times an independent lognormal multiplier with median 1 and rate_sd as the standard deviation of its logarithm.

The trait is then Brownian motion on the tree whose branch lengths are multiplied by their rates, drawn at the tips and then at the internal nodes given the tips, as in trait_bm().

References

Rabosky, D. L. (2014). Automatic detection of key innovations, rate shifts, and diversity-dependence on phylogenetic trees. PLoS ONE, 9, e89543. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0089543

Eastman, J. M., Alfaro, M. E., Joyce, P., Hipp, A. L., & Harmon, L. J. (2011). A novel comparative method for identifying shifts in the rate of character evolution on trees. Evolution, 65, 3578–3589. doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.2011.01401.x

Martin, B. S., Bradburd, G. S., Harmon, L. J., & Weber, M. G. (2023). Modeling the evolution of rates of continuous trait evolution. Systematic Biology, 72, 590–605. doi:10.1093/sysbio/syac068

Revell, L. J. (2021). A variable-rate quantitative trait evolution model using penalized-likelihood. PeerJ, 9, e11997. doi:10.7717/peerj.11997

Thomas, G. H., & Freckleton, R. P. (2012). MOTMOT: models of trait macroevolution on trees. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 3, 145–151. doi:10.1111/j.2041-210X.2011.00132.x

See also

trait_bm() for a single rate, trait_mk() for discrete traits with rates that vary among branches.

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), food_web_rates(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), plot_traits(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), species_traits(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_mk(), trait_ou(), turnover_rates()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
x <- trait_rates(tr, "shift", shifts = 1, shift_size = 8)
x$shifts
#>   edge node position multiplier rate
#> 1   38   20        0          8    8
head(x$tips)
#>         t1         t2         t3         t4         t5         t6 
#>  0.3876716  0.3725845  0.1821453 -0.3773427 -0.5333873 -0.5354236 
# shifts as a Poisson process, each new regime with a rate of its own, as in BAMM
b <- trait_rates(tr, "shift", shift_rate = 0.1, relative = FALSE,
                 shift_size = function(n) stats::rexp(n))
b$shifts
#> [1] edge       node       position   multiplier rate      
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
g <- trait_rates(tr, "gbm", rate_sd = 0.5)
summary(g$edge_rates)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.3990  0.7932  0.8618  0.8986  0.9967  1.7629 
# as the environmental optima of a metacommunity
traits <- species_traits(tr, optima = g$tips)
